🟢 [health] steer-001 stands: ai-trader-pending is 23T 7W 30.4% net -$0.37 over 7d (20 of 23 SHORT, 3 scratch), 4 consecutive losses — and the open BTC position belongs to this family. AI_TRADER_ENABLED=False only gates the hourly pick; manually-armed pendings remain the live path.

🟢 [info] hourly pick fired this cycle (slot open, prior pick 66min old): ME SHORT — precheck PASS all gates, watchlist-only because AI_TRADER_ENABLED=False.

Direction right, protection wrong — same verdict as last cycle, an hour further along. The BTC short sits on the aligned side of a 935-bar below-EMA300 structure and is +6.5% on margin, but the stop has never moved in 5.9 hours. That is the whole risk, because of what this exact position historically is: in the last 7 days, ai-trader-pending BTC shorts that armed (MFE ≥0.40) all came back through the stop — 0.778 → manual_sl_hit, 0.871 → hard_max_loss, 0.517 → manual_sl_hit. Three armed shorts, three givebacks, zero kept. We are in the giveback cell, and the entry cell is already paid for. The trail-step steer is the cheapest possible fix and its condition has only strengthened (54 → 82 closes under 67322).

Fresh entry today? No — 93.5% of 7d gross loss comes from trades that never reached +0.40% MFE, and the 7d split is brutal in both directions: never-armed 48T 5W 10.4% WR -$4.01 vs armed 45T 38W 84.4% WR +$2.09. The next entry is statistically a never-armed loser. So: hold the existing short, do not add, and manage — do not open fresh discretionary positions. The ME SHORT pick is watchlist-only and explicitly conditional (invalid if BTC reclaims EMA300 15-30m or ME's own regime flips LONG).

Would I open each fresh today? BTC SHORT: no — not at +6.5% off the low with the giveback history above; I would only be holding what I already have, with the stop at 67322. SOL SHORT: marginal yes on structure and meta_rsi 60.6 (center of the short band), but its own 5m regime is NEUTRAL (conf 42.3) and it entered into an active BTC bounce — hold the existing stop (76.032), no add, same EMA300-reclaim invalidation as the cluster steer.

What the winning side looked like on the standing 7d losers (no new closes this cycle): structure won six — SHORTs beat the JUP/INJ/IOTA LONGs held under a below-EMA300 BTC; extremes lost the other way — the meta_rsi-88 BTC LONG and meta_rsi-92 CFX SHORT were placed where extension beat reversal (the BANANA lesson, mirrored). Six of eight never armed. None of them was an exit-management failure: they were entries against already-decided structure, or extremes traded as magnets instead of springs. The adverse change this cycle is momentum, not structure: zscore recovered to +0.19, 1m/5m linreg now fractionally positive (15m/1h still negative), and short-breadth halved twice in 30 minutes — the classic chop tape that converted those three armed BTC shorts into manual exits. Argument for locking, not for exiting.

That combination — structure down, momentum up, labels swinging hourly — is CHOP, which is exactly what auto_trader says and exactly where our history says we lose.
